subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` adopt a new 1 MiB public maximum, or should it retain existing readable-file compatibility while resource handling is redesigned around an approved contract?
rationale: The fixed cap changes user-visible acceptance behavior, but the supplied source, tests, and PR discussion do not show an existing documented limit or a downstream contract that mandates 1 MiB.

options.title: Preserve current compatibility
options.body: Remove the default 1 MiB rejection and return with a bounded approach only after its user-facing contract and downstream constraint are established.

options.title: Adopt the cap deliberately
options.body: Approve 1 MiB as the public limit, document the compatibility change, repair the path race, and require live evidence for all affected input classes.

recommendation.title: Preserve current compatibility
recommendation.body: Remove the default 1 MiB rejection and return with a bounded approach only after its user-facing contract and downstream constraint are established.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline directly routes review attention to steipete, and the remaining blocker is product-contract ownership rather than a contributor-only mechanical change.
